content:
incident-bot: PAGER - Multi-region failover started for us-east-1 -> eu-west-1. Detected by healthchecks: regional control plane reported increased 5xxs and connection errors. Auto-traffic-shift invoked at 2930456789
ajay-oncall: paging oncall. I'm on it. seeing console alerts, load balancer saturation in us-east-1
maria-sre: I'm awake, joining. what's current traffic split?
ajay-oncall: controller shows traffic_shift: us-east-1 40%, eu-west-1 60% but many connections still sticky to us-east due to long ALB keepalives
jamie-net: we're also seeing DNS TTLs of 300s for internal service discovery — that's preventing quick client switchover
maria-sre: confirmed. healthcheck logs show envoy returning 503 from backend pool 'gpu-pool-us-east-1' with 'upstream connection reset'
ajay-oncall: impact assessment: Dedicated customers in us-east-1 experiencing 10-60% request failures depending on session stickiness. Hosted API retries mitigating some, but latency spike for many requests. marking P1
lisa-pm: flagged to CS. Which customers hit hardest? need external comms if SLA risk
maria-sre: initial query: `SELECT customer_id, error_rate FROM telemetry WHERE region='us-east-1' AND last_5m > 0.1` shows 12 customers above 10% errors, 3 above 40%
ajay-oncall: mitigation path 1: attempt graceful drain of us-east nodes and force traffic shift to eu-west-1. mitigation path 2: rollback traffic-shift and restore us-east routing if drain fails. prefer drain+shift
ops-bot: runbook step 2: `redwoodctl traffic-shift --from us-east-1 --to eu-west-1 --target-percent 100 --grace-period 300`
maria-sre: running that now, will watch KV cache evictions. logs:
```
[2026-03-15T02:13:10Z] traffic-shift: 40% -> 60% -> 80% (stalled at 80%)
[2026-03-15T02:14:02Z] drain: stuck waiting for connections to drop, active sessions 1821
[2026-03-15T02:14:15Z] envoy: route-by-header sticky-session fallback engaged
```
ajay-oncall: looks like sticky sessions are preventing drain. we need to invalidate session affinity or reduce keepalive on ALB
jamie-net: ALB config shows `stickiness.enabled=true` and cookie ttl 24h. I can toggle stickiness off but that will cause some 5xx as clients reconnect. recommend toggling on small window
maria-sre: do it. switch stickiness to false on the target pool, and set session-ttl to 20s temporarily
jamie-net: running:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay_timeout_seconds,Value=30
```
ops-bot: change applied
maria-sre: traffic shift resumed: 90% -> 100%. monitoring error rates
ajay-oncall: good. reducing DNS TTL to 30s to accelerate client-side switchover for B2B customers that use DNS caching
lisa-pm: CS drafted message to affected customers: short outage, mitigation in progress, ETA 20m
maria-sre: we've also identified a routecache bug where `routecache.Update()` ignores invalidation when traffic-shift is forced — filed internal issue RDW-4821. For the short term we pushed a hotfix to the control plane to force KV cache flush
ajay-oncall: hotfix applied. validation checks: `curl -v http://internal-health-us-east-1/ping` returns 404 then 200 — ok
maria-sre: error rates dropping: high-error customers back to baseline within last 4m. still watching for residual 502s from long-lived streams
jamie-net: running cross-region perf tests for egress bandwidth, seems stable
ajay-oncall: oncall handoff: I'm pausing now. maria, taking over active monitoring for the next 2h? I'll be reachable but switching to standby
maria-sre: taking handoff. will escalate if metrics degrade >2x baseline or any single customer >5% error for 10m
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated, mitigation=traffic_shift_complete_and_cache_flush, severity=P1 -> P2, duration=~27m
lisa-pm: great work team. next steps: postmortem to include root cause of routecache invalidation and DNS TTL defaults, add runbook step to disable long ALB stickiness during forced failover
ajay-oncall: agree. I'll start incident timeline and assign RDW-4821 to jamie and RDW-4822 to infra to update default TTLs
maria-sre: leaving a note: checkdedicated customers with pinned model versions — we need a follow-up to ensure model-serving sessions correctly reconnect after cross-region moves
ajay-oncall: thanks all. closing thread, will link postmortem when complete :thumbsup:
